## Why visit

A particularly efficient excursion for beer travellers because it is close to both Wigan stations and delivers a distinctive railway-arch setting alongside serious ale and cider. The railway-inspired rooms and train departure displays are useful atmosphere rather than the entire reason to visit: the changing beer range and international bottle selection can sustain a long tasting session. Together with the Swan & Railway it makes a compact, high-value pair of stops. Look beyond the visible taps and ask about bottles if you want something unusual or a shared contrast to cask.

## Beer

Official site advertises seven changing real ales and a broad bottle range; current choices are linked from its live board. Its regular Signal house bitter is brewed by Bank Top (based on Flat Cap); recent changing casks include Brass Castle Bad Kitty and Bank Top Hercules.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA marks real cider; the venue specialises in ale and cider and advertises a changing cider selection. Verify the individual pour. CAMRA reports rotating draught ciders and perries without fixing one producer or product.

## Plan the visit

Sunday live music is advertised, so choose timing to suit conversation versus entertainment. Do not infer November beers from today’s board.

**Getting there:** Very close to Wigan North Western and Wigan Wallgate stations.
